question: You are using Claude Code in one long session to fix four bugs from your tracker. Each bug has a ticket ID, an affected file, a count of failing tests, and a status. After the conversation was compacted, Claude mixed up which failing test count belonged to which ticket and described the statuses only vaguely. Which changes best preserve this per-bug information for the rest of the session?

options.text: Paste the complete raw test output for all four bugs into every new message so that no detail can be lost.
options.reason: Verbose outputs accumulate in context and consume tokens out of proportion to their relevance; the guide recommends keeping only the relevant fields.

options.text: Ask Claude to merge all four bugs into one short prose recap paragraph and rely on that recap for the later steps.
options.reason: A prose recap is a vague summary that mixes the issues together; the guide recommends structured, separately persisted issue data instead.

options.text: Keep a structured record per bug with its ticket ID, file, failing test count, and status in a scratchpad file, and update it after each fix.
options.reason: Persisting structured issue data in a separate layer, such as a scratchpad file, keeps each bug's exact facts apart from summarized history in a multi-issue session.

options.text: Include a structured facts block that lists each ticket ID, file, failing test count, and status in every prompt, outside the summarized history.
options.reason: A persistent facts block kept outside summarized history prevents progressive summarization from blurring the numbers and statuses of each issue.

options.text: Run /compact more often so that the summarized history stays short and Claude can focus on the bug it is fixing now.
options.reason: More summarization increases the progressive summarization risk: exact numbers and statuses are condensed into vague summaries, which caused the problem.
